clue.text: Your band flopping? 'That's the limit!

indicators.note: a band that is flopping falls apart, so its letters with those of 'your' are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fed-up fan watches their group fail and declares they have had enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flopping' rearranges the letters of YOUR BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: A boundary is a limit, and the exclamation points at the edge beyond which one may not go.

clue.text: Picking up vehicle, takes unusual driving position — that's critical

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A taxi driver collects a car and drives it in an odd posture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picking up' turns CAB into BAC; 'unusual' rearranges TAKES to KSEAT. The definition points to the critical backseat driver.
explanation.definitionFit: A backseat driver criticises from the rear, so the back seat is the critic's driving position.

clue.text: Measures of alcohol for military teams

definitions.meaning: standard amounts of drink used to count intake
detachments or groups of soldiers in an army

explanation.definitionFit: Units are both the standard measures of alcohol consumption and military detachments.

clue.text: Clutching thin album does suggest one that's highly musical

indicators.note: one piece clutching others holds them inside

parts.note: female deer are does, so does are deer
scant means thin or meagre
an album is a record

explanation.surface: Someone gripping a slim LP hints at a person with soaring musical talent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does' is the plural of doe, not the verb; DEER clutches SCANT RECORD.
explanation.definitionFit: The descant recorder is the high-pitched soprano member of the recorder family.

clue.text: Elegant, but penalised again

parts.note: RE is a prefix meaning again
someone fined has been penalised

explanation.surface: A stylish person is nonetheless punished a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined manners or taste are polished and cultivated, a synonym of elegant.

clue.text: Child's word not bought by Daddy

definitions.text: Child's word not bought by Daddy

parts.words: Child's word not bought by Daddy
parts.note: a nursery word for a dog, recalling the Victorian music-hall song in which a child laments that Daddy wouldn't buy one

explanation.walkthrough: The music-hall song 'Daddy Wouldn't Buy Me a ...' is a British popular song of the 1890s; the child's word is the nursery name for a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Small children call a dog by imitating its bark, and the old song is about a dog Daddy refused to buy.

clue.text: At sea, so allocate cabin furniture

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: On a voyage, a steward assigns a passenger a cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' rearranges SO ALLOCATE CABIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An occasional table is a small piece of furniture used as needed, an example of furniture.

clue.text: With slowing of tempo, Elgar arrangement is exaggerated

parts.note: rit is short for ritardando, the musical direction to slow down

indicators.note: a musical arrangement reworks a piece, so the composer's name is rearranged

explanation.surface: A slower-paced version of an Elgar piece is overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' turns ELGAR into LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Writ large means magnified or in an exaggerated form, as something made more obvious.

clue.text: Small dish is sad to see

parts.note: wee means small
a pie is a dish

explanation.surface: A tiny plate of food is a depressing sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a film that is sad to see.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is a sentimental film or story that moves its audience to tears.

clue.text: Beach artist, is she?

parts.note: a beach is made of sand
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a beach painter is a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sandra is a woman's given name, so it can stand for a particular she.

clue.text: Brief reason I entered college

indicators.note: one letter going into another word is said to have entered it
a brief word is cut short, so the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: A short explanation for why someone got into a university college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' cuts CAUSE to CAUS, and 'entered' puts I inside it. Gonville and Caius is a Cambridge college, usually called simply Caius.
explanation.definitionFit: Caius is the common short name of Gonville and Caius, one of the Cambridge University colleges.

clue.text: Anatole secures his vote

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one name contains the other word

parts.note: Anatole France was the French novelist and Nobel laureate

explanation.surface: A man named Anatole manages to win his ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatole France (1844-1924) was a French writer; his surname holds HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: The franchise is the right to vote in elections, as in the extension of the franchise to women.

clue.text: Hear stammerer's marked as bore

indicators.note: an instruction to listen, so the words are taken by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: someone who stammers would say the word for marked, stained, with a stuttered first letter

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a stutterer whose speech is noted as tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is the past tense of bear, as in bore a weight, not a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to sustain it, so the past tense bore matches the past tense of sustain.

clue.text: Fish not on, I got game dish

indicators.note: the word on is not kept, so it is removed from the fish

parts.note: salmon is a fish

explanation.surface: Someone skips the fish course and is served a dish of game instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' takes ON out of SALMON, leaving SALM.
explanation.definitionFit: A salmi is a ragout of roasted game birds such as partridge or pheasant, finished in a rich sauce.

clue.text: Retired, keeping dry — back of stove helped

indicators.note: one piece keeping others holds them inside it

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed, so is abed
TT stands for teetotal, meaning dry or abstaining from alcohol

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone went to bed sober, and the rear of the cooker came in handy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' here means gone to bed, not stopped working; 'dry' is the crossword's teetotal, and 'back of' takes the final letter of 'stove'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage, so abetted is a synonym of helped, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Outdoor theatre amazingly used up air

indicators.note: something done amazingly is done in a surprising way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An open-air venue has exhausted its supply of oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amazingly' rearranges USED UP AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidaurus in Greece has a famous ancient open-air theatre with remarkable acoustics.

clue.text: Notice about pig on deck

indicators.note: one word put about another goes around it

parts.note: an advertisement or notice is an ad
a boar is a male pig

explanation.surface: A sign is posted about a pig that is loose on a ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on deck' is the definition, meaning on board ship, not a pack of cards or a waiting batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being aboard a ship means being on it, so on deck is an equivalent phrase.

clue.text: Hm, sit down in front there!

definitions.meaning: a hesitating murmur while thinking something over
a theatregoer's complaint to someone blocking the view

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a pause for thought and a plea to have the view cleared.

clue.text: With sharp implement, not hard to cure this gland

parts.note: a pin is a sharp implement

indicators.note: the letter for hard is not wanted, so it is removed

parts.note: to heal is to cure
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A doctor proposes treating a gland with a needle rather than harsh methods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes H from HEAL, leaving EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineal is a small gland in the brain that produces melatonin.

clue.text: Feeble, half-formed notion, that's clear

parts.note: limp means feeble or weak

indicators.note: only half of the word is formed, so it loses its second half

parts.note: a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: A weak, incomplete thought is somehow lucid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-formed' cuts IDEA to ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Limpid means transparent or lucid, as of water or prose that is clear.

clue.text: Twin cats?

parts.note: describes a breed of cat from Thailand which also gave its name to conjoined twins

explanation.definitionFit: Siamese is both a breed of cat and the old name for conjoined twins, so one word covers both.

clue.text: Not so happy keeping in line he'll offer you a seat

indicators.note: to keep something in is to hold it inside, so one word goes into another

parts.note: sadder means less happy

explanation.surface: A gloomier man stays in the queue and offers a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: The seat is a horse's saddle, not a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A saddler makes and sells saddles, the seats used in horse riding.

clue.text: Well, having beaten 'flu, but not steady

parts.note: fit means well or healthy

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is healthy again after getting over influenza, but still unsteady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' rearranges FLU into FUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitful means irregular or intermittent, as fitful sleep that is not steady.

clue.text: Comma perhaps adds nothing to one journal

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a magazine or journal is a mag
O looks like zero, meaning nothing

explanation.surface: A punctuation mark contributes nothing to a periodical.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is a butterfly, not punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the adult winged stage of an insect, and the comma butterfly is one example.

clue.text: Fast road, fancy, blocked by stone: no place to remount

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, written MI in crosswords

indicators.note: a word blocked by another has that other stuck in its middle

parts.note: a fancy or fantasy is a dream
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: On a motorway, a daydream is interrupted by a rock; there is nowhere to get back on.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is London to Leeds, Britain's first motorway. The definition plays on the saying 'don't change horses in midstream'.
explanation.definitionFit: Changing horses midstream is proverbially unwise, so it is no place to mount a fresh horse.

clue.text: Heath, raised area of land I entered

indicators.note: a letter that has entered a word sits inside it
in a down clue, raised means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an acre is an area of land

explanation.surface: A heath is an elevated tract of land that someone walked into.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns ACRE into ERCA, and 'entered' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers, so the plant name means heath.

clue.text: Shot by stream in emergency exercise

parts.note: a gun that has shot has fired
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Someone is shot down beside a brook during a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire drill is a practice evacuation, rehearsing what to do in an emergency.

clue.text: Small mistakes by bachelor what to kiss?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
lips are what one kisses

explanation.surface: A single man makes minor errors and wonders where to kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Blips are minor glitches or temporary errors, small slips in an otherwise steady course.

clue.text: One with strong desire, say, for glory

indicators.note: an invitation to speak the word, so it is matched by sound

parts.note: someone who lusts is a luster

explanation.surface: Someone with a powerful craving speaks out for fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is brilliance or distinction, as in adding lustre to a reputation, a synonym of glory.

clue.text: Cocaine at zero charge, or low

parts.note: something at no cost is free
base means low or mean

explanation.surface: Drugs on offer for nothing, which is a contemptible thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Freebase is a purified form of cocaine prepared for smoking.
